sections.title: Why this module matters
sections.body: TypeScript is the standard in professional React and Angular projects, and any company using it will test whether you understand basic type annotations, interfaces, generics, and union types. As a Java developer, you already understand the value of static typing — TypeScript brings that discipline to JavaScript. The exam-critical difference is that TypeScript uses structural typing (shape compatibility), not Java's nominal typing (explicit class hierarchy).

sections.title: Mental model
sections.body:
- **TypeScript = JavaScript + types at compile time**: all type annotations are erased when compiled to JS. No type checks at runtime.
- **Structural typing**: if an object has the required properties, it satisfies the type — no `implements` keyword needed (unlike Java).
- **`type` vs `interface`**: prefer `interface` for object shapes (supports declaration merging and `extends`); `type` for unions, primitives, and tuples.
- **Generics**: same concept as Java generics — `Array<T>`, `Promise<T>`, `Record<K,V>`. Constraints use `extends` keyword.
- **Union types** (`A | B`): TypeScript's killer feature — a value can be one of several types, and you narrow it with guards.
- **Strict null checks**: with `strictNullChecks: true`, `null` and `undefined` are not in every type's domain — you must explicitly handle them.

sections.title: Must-know concepts
sections.body:
- **typescript-vs-javascript**: why TypeScript, what `tsc` does, what type erasure means.
- **types-and-interfaces**: know primitive types, `type` alias, `interface`, and the 3-4 key differences between them.
- **union-intersection-types**: `A | B` union, `A & B` intersection, discriminated unions for state machines.
- **generics-basics**: write a generic function and constrain with `extends`.
- **type-narrowing**: `typeof`, `instanceof`, `in` operator guards, and custom type predicates.
- **optional-chaining-nullish-coalescing**: `?.` and `??` — know these cold, they appear constantly in React code.

sections.title: Likely interview hooks
sections.body:
- *"What is the difference between `type` and `interface` in TypeScript?"* — interfaces support declaration merging and class `implements`; type aliases can express unions, tuples, and mapped types.
- *"What is structural typing?"* — TypeScript checks shape compatibility, not class identity. Two different classes with the same properties are considered compatible.
- *"What is a discriminated union?"* — a union of types where each member has a literal field (`kind`, `type`) that uniquely identifies which variant it is, enabling exhaustive type narrowing.
- *"How do generics in TypeScript compare to Java generics?"* — similar concept but TypeScript's are structural and erased at runtime; Java uses type erasure too but has bounded wildcards TypeScript handles via `extends`.
- *"What does `?.` do?"* — optional chaining: returns `undefined` if any link in the chain is null/undefined instead of throwing.

sections.title: Speaking template
sections.body: > *"TypeScript adds a compile-time type layer on top of JavaScript. Coming from Java, the main mental shift is that TypeScript uses structural typing — if an object has the right properties and methods, it satisfies the type, regardless of what class it belongs to. This means I can describe the shape of an API response with an interface, and any object matching that shape will be accepted. At runtime, all type information is erased, so TypeScript gives you safety during development without any runtime overhead."*
